findings.summary: operatorChannel.tokenHash is returned by GET /api/config, contradicting the documented guarantee
findings.recommendation: Instance. docs/configuration-reference.md and docs/operator-channel.md say the token hash is never returned by any route. But GET /api/config (and the other _withBindState caller near server.js:2234) sends the whole config through redactConfigSecrets, which strips deletePassword, basicAuthHash and serviceToken and does not touch operatorChannel. So any caller that can read config gets operatorChannel.tokenHash. The hash of a 256-bit random token cannot be used to authenticate, so this is not exploitable. The problem is the false claim and the break from the repo's own convention for secrets in config. Fix it in redactConfigSecrets, the one function all config output passes through: drop operatorChannel.tokenHash and expose tokenConfigured, as status() already does. Add an operator GET /api/config assertion to test/api-operator-channel.test.js.

findings.summary: Replies are checked against the current target, but waiting messages keep their original target
findings.recommendation: Instance. Each inbound row keeps target_project_id, so after a target change the pump still delivers waiting messages to the old project, as documented. resolveOutbound in lib/operator-channel.js, however, marks a reply relayable only when sent.sender_project_id equals the current settings.targetProject. The old project's inReplyTo answers to messages TangleClaw delivered on purpose are therefore quarantined as not-from-target-project, their text is dropped, and the operator never sees them. When sent.in_reply_to maps to an inbound row, accept a sender equal to that row's target_project_id. Use the current target only for replies that answer nothing. Add a target-change round-trip test (none exists).

findings.summary: Fifty pending messages for an offline project hold back every other project
findings.recommendation: Instance. _pumpPass reads listPendingInbound(50), which is the oldest 50 pending rows, and only afterwards skips projects already waiting. If the oldest 50 are for an offline project, later rows for a live project are never listed, so they wait until the offline project comes back. docs/operator-channel.md says 'Messages for other projects still go.' This is easy to reach: at 20 messages a minute an offline target builds up 50 in under three minutes, and changing the target then starves the new one. Fix it with a query that returns the oldest pending row per target project, or one that pages past waiting projects. Test it with more than 50 rows for an offline project ahead of a live one.

findings.summary: A crash after a bound send but before settleInbound reports send_unknown for a known-sent message
findings.recommendation: Instance. If sendTracked returned 200 and bound a hub id but the process died before settleInbound, the retry under the same requestId gets SEND_ALREADY_ATTEMPTED and is recorded as send_unknown, although its exchange is 'sent'. No duplicate is sent, so this is only a less precise record. If precision matters, read the exchange named in details.exchangeId and settle as 'sent' with its hub id when it is bound.

observations.summary: Emoji with a variation selector or ZWJ are refused inbound and quarantined outbound
observations.recommendation: Instance. isSafeChannelText delegates to workload.isSafeText, whose UNSAFE_TEXT refuses \p{Cf} and \p{Default_Ignorable_Code_Point}. That set includes U+FE0F and U+200D, which common chat emoji carry (a red heart, a thumbs-up with a skin tone, or any ZWJ sequence). An operator message containing one gets 400 UNSAFE_TEXT, and an agent reply containing one is quarantined as unsafe-text with its text dropped, which the operator never sees. test/operator-channel.test.js pins 'e\uFE0F' as unsafe, so this is deliberate under A29/A30. If it is intended, ACCEPT it and say so in docs/operator-channel.md. Otherwise, ask the Architect whether emoji presentation selectors and ZWJ may be allowed in chat text, as line breaks and tabs already are.

Instance. In 'lets only a signed-in operator configure the channel or mint its token', the assertion moved from status === 403 to 401 || 403.
